- No render was refused.. Judge: I judged 4 pairs, and the commercial (GTA V) frame clearly wins every one; none is close. The in-development game has a clear identity: a Singapore-like harbour with landmark homages, a warm afternoon colour grade, several boats with white wakes, mirror-like reflections of the skyline in the water, and ripple rings from the rotor downwash. Its density at mid distance is reasonable. It loses consistently on six points. (1) The helicopter, the playable vehicle here, has a near-black, low-detail body, and its rotors render as dark translucent wedges or ellipses that look like artifacts. (2) The water is a uniform teal, with no colour change by depth, no transparency, no surf against the shore or structures, and foam that looks like flat blotches. (3) Materials are weak: boxy towers with repeating window grids, and piers, grass and park structures that are flat slabs. (4) The images are milky and low in contrast, without the layered haze that gives a sense of distance. (5) The camera either looks down from above or crops the subject, and a large HUD and empty minimap cover the skyline. (6) The character on foot has little detail and a stiff, arms-down idle pose. One caveat: the reference frames are hand-picked press shots with no HUD, which makes the gap look bigger. But even with the HUD removed, the in-development frames would lose every pair. These are still images, so they cannot show walking or running animation; only the stiff standing pose in pair 3 is visible. The fixes with the most effect, in order: rotors drawn as light motion blur instead of a dark disc, plus glossy helicopter materials (this is the playable vehicle); water that changes colour with depth and breaks into surf at the shore; haze that layers the distance; and a better-detailed, better-framed character on foot.
